swiftlet.snapshot_orientation.cell_shifts_in_cells(cell_shift, nr_cells_axis)[source]

Convert the tables cell shift from multiples of 1/8 to number of cells.

Returns the shift in cells, np.ndarray of int64, shape (3,).

Parameters:

  • cell_shift (array-like of int, shape (3,)) – shift along x, y and z, in eighths of the box

  • nr_cells_axis (int or array-like of int, shape (3,)) – number of cells along each axis of the snapshot, a multiple of 8

swiftlet.snapshot_orientation.check_neighbouring_tiles(tables, nr_cells_axis, orientation_lock=None, orientation_seed=0, extent=3, warn=True, boxsize=None, shell=None)[source]

Returns a NeighbourTileReport after checking for clashing tiles from the orientation table.

Check orientation tables for cells that touch their own copy in a neighbouring tile as a cell sharing a face with its own copy puts the same structures side by side.

Only neighbouring tiles that are oriented differently can lead to replicas of the same cell have touching, e.g., with orientation_lock=”cube” pairs of cells can touch only be touching on the faces between layers.

This method is quicker and coarser than swiftlet.repeat_check.find_close_cell_repeats, which builds the actual lightcone shell of a simulation and also finds copies close along a line of sight.

Due to only doing a course check orientation_lock=”sphere” cannot be used with this method as it requires a more complete rebuild of the lightcone. To test with Sphere use swiftlet.repeat_check.find_close_cell_repeats

Parameters:

  • tables (dict or str) – orientation tables, as a dict (see check_orientation_tables) or the path of a table file (see write_orientation_tables)

  • nr_cells_axis (int) – number of SWIFT cells along each axis of the snapshots, e.g. 32 for FLAMINGO

  • orientation_lock (str) – None (or “none”) or “cube”. “sphere” splits tiles between layers by distance, which needs the lightcone: use find_close_cell_repeats

  • orientation_seed (int) – seed of the tile orientations

  • extent (int) – check the tiles (nx, ny, nz) with |nx|, |ny|, |nz| <= extent

  • warn (boolean) – if True, warn (swiftlet.repeat_check.CloseRepeatWarning) if cells touch their copy

  • shell (tuple) – (minimum, maximum) comoving distance [Mpc] of a lightcone shell. If given, only touching copies whose cells overlap the shell are kept

swiftlet.snapshot_orientation.check_orientation_tables(tables)[source]

Check orientation tables.

Three tables with the same number of rows (at least 1) of 3 whole numbers to build new snapshot tiles:

  • the quarter turns about the x, y and z axes

  • reflections of +1 or -1 per axis

  • periodic shifts in eighths of the box per axis and in EIGHTH_SHIFT_VALUES

The tables can also hold “cell_shift_unit”, which must be “eighths”.

Returns the tables as a dict.

Parameters:

tables (dict) – {“QuarterTurns”, “Reflections”, “CellShifts”}

swiftlet.snapshot_orientation.default_orientation_tables(name='default_v2')[source]

The orientation table reverted to when no orientation table is given, these tables are installed with SWIFTLET.

By default the current default tables (DEFAULT_ORIENTATION_TABLE); “default_v2” gives the first default tables.

Returns the tables as a dict, see check_orientation_tables.

Parameters:

name (str) – name of the installed tables, one of INSTALLED_ORIENTATION_TABLES

swiftlet.snapshot_orientation.generate_clash_free_tables(seed=21, nr_cells_axis=16, cell_shift_values=(0, 1, -1, 2, -2, 3, -3, 4), shuffle_seed=0)[source]

Generate an orientation table that doesn’t allow for replica cells to be touching.

Orientation tables in which no two rows clash: no cell touches its own copy across the face between two neighbouring tiles, whichever two rows the tiles take, for any orientation_lock and orientation_seed. The cell shifts are in eighths of the box, so the clashes are the same for every number of cells per axis that is a multiple of 8 and at least 16 (checked for 16, 32 and 64), and one table serves every such simulation.

Every candidate is one of the distinct orientations (48 turns and reflections, times the shifts along each axis, generate_orientation_tables). Starting from the unchanged box, the rows are chosen in rounds, one for each of the 48 turns and reflections per round, at random, skipping rows that clash with one already chosen; then every turn and reflection is cut down to the same number of rows, choosing the rows that keep the shifts along each axis even. The first row is the unchanged box, and the others are shuffled. The same arguments give the same tables. This is how the installed default_v2 tables were made (seed 21, the most even of seeds 4 to 63; see tools/make_default_orientation_tables.py).

Returns the tables as a dict, see check_orientation_tables.

Parameters:

  • seed (int) – seed of the random order in which the rows are chosen

  • nr_cells_axis (int) – number of cells per axis the clashes are found for (16 gives those of 32 and 64 too)

  • cell_shift_values (sequence of int) – shifts each axis can take, in eighths of the box

  • shuffle_seed (int) – seed of the shuffle of the rows after the first, and of the choice between equally even rows

swiftlet.snapshot_orientation.generate_orientation_tables(seed=0, n_rows=None, cell_shift_values=(0, 1, -1, 2, -2, 3, -3, 4))[source]

Build an orientation table.

Orientation tables holding every distinct orientation: each of the 48 ways of turning and reflecting the box (the signed permutations of the axes) with each combination of the cell shifts along x, y and z, e.g. 48 x 7^3 = 16464 rows for the default shifts. The first row leaves the box unchanged, so the observer’s box tile (0, 0, 0) is not re-oriented with orientation_seed=0, and the other rows are shuffled.

Returns the tables as a dict, see check_orientation_tables.

Parameters:

  • seed (int) – seed of the shuffle of the rows, the same seed gives the same tables

  • n_rows (int) – number of rows to keep (the first, unchanged, and n_rows - 1 others). If None, all

  • cell_shift_values (sequence of int) – shifts each axis can take, including 0, in 1/8 of the box

swiftlet.snapshot_orientation.installed_orientation_table_file(name='default_v2')[source]

swiftlet.snapshot_orientation.rotate_coords_cartesian(coords, rot_angles, reflections=None, periodic_shift=None, sidelengths=None, order='xyz', degrees=False, out=None, inplace=False, invert=False)[source]

Rotate Cartesian coordinates about the x, y, z axes.

Uses a numba-compiled, parallelized loop when numba is available and falls back to NumPy matmul otherwise.

Returns the rotated coordinates, shape (N, 3).

Parameters:

  • coords (np.ndarray) – coordinates, shape (N, 3)

  • rot_angles (array-like, shape (3,)) – (angle_x, angle_y, angle_z), radians unless degrees=True

  • reflections (array-like, shape (3,)) – per-axis reflection signs (+1/-1). Pass None for no reflection

  • periodic_shift (array-like of int, shape (3,)) – shift along x, y, z. Must be given with sidelengths

  • sidelengths (float or array-like, shape (3,)) – side length of the snapshot box (scalar for cubic, or (3,))

  • order (str) – rotation composition order, a permutation of “x”, “y”, “z”

  • degrees (boolean) – If True, then angles are given in degrees

  • out (np.ndarray) – preallocated output buffer, shape (N, 3) (avoids reallocation on repeated calls)

  • inplace (boolean) – If True, overwrite coords in place instead of allocating new memory

  • invert (boolean) – If True, apply the inverse of the rotation and periodic shift. Requires periodic_shift

swiftlet.snapshot_orientation.tables_are_clash_free(tables, nr_cells_axis=16)[source]

Check that an orientation table will not produce touching cell replicas.

Check that no two rows of orientation tables (nor a row with itself) make a cell touch its own copy across the face between neighbouring tiles.

Returns the number of clashing (row, row) pairs, 0 if the tables are clash-free.

Parameters:

  • tables (dict) – orientation tables, see check_orientation_tables

  • nr_cells_axis (int) – number of cells along each axis

swiftlet.snapshot_orientation.write_orientation_tables(filename, tables=None, seed=0, n_rows=None, cell_shift_values=(0, 1, -1, 2, -2, 3, -3, 4), attributes=None)[source]

Write orientation tables to a YAML file. The tables are given, or generated with every distinct orientation.

The .hdf5 file holds the datasets ‘QuarterTurns’, ‘Reflections’ and ‘CellShifts’, and the attributes describing them

Returns the fingerprint of the tables.

Parameters:

  • filename (str) – path of the file to write, .yaml or .yml

  • tables (dict) – tables to write, see check_orientation_tables. If None, generate them

  • seed (int) – seed of generate_orientation_tables, if the tables are generated

  • n_rows (int) – number of rows of generate_orientation_tables, if the tables are generated

  • cell_shift_values (sequence of int) – cell shifts of generate_orientation_tables, if the tables are generated

class swiftlet.snapshot_orientation.NeighbourTileReport(nr_neighbour_pairs, nr_reoriented_pairs, touching, shell=None)[source]

Bases: object

The result of check_neighbouring_tiles.

nr_neighbour_pairs: number of pairs of tiles sharing a face that were checked nr_reoriented_pairs: number of those pairs whose two tiles have different orientations nr_touching_pairs: number of pairs of tiles in which some cell touches its own copy across the shared face nr_touching_cells: number of cells touching their own copy, over every pair of tiles touching: every cell touching its own copy: a dict of arrays “tile_a” and “tile_b” (N, 3), the

two tiles, and “cell”, the cell’s index, (i * n + j) * n + k for the cell (i, j, k) of a box of n cells per axis, as SWIFT numbers them

shell: the shell [Mpc] the touching cells were kept in, or None for whole tiles
